slides.title: Can a model learn useful steps for an unfamiliar task?
slides.notes:
Long-term question: useful decomposition and delegation. Immediate question: teach actions that follow from what the learner has seen.

The main result is teaching repair, not proof that recursion helps. See the reading guide for the whole story.

slides.title: A crafting game makes the outcome easy to check.
slides.notes:
Toy example, not a measured task. Two sticks make one frame. Frame plus glowing stone makes one lantern. Recipes must be looked up.

Native inventory checks success. A fluent explanation without the item is a failure. Real item names are unfamiliar codes.

slides.title: We test two ways of teaching the model.
slides.notes:
SFT supplies the next action in a worked example. RL supplies a reward for a completed attempt. Both change model weights.

Looking up a recipe during evaluation is not weight training. Our RL starts from an SFT-trained model.

slides.title: We changed the information shown before the action.
slides.notes:
Repair reschedules existing recipe queries and rebuilds histories. It uses a known solution. The same 366 answer strings and 23 updates remain.

Input histories and lengths change. We have not isolated why the repair helps. Frame and lantern are simplified labels.

slides.title: The repair helped after retraining and on more goals.
slides.notes:
Scores: 1 to 14, 2 to 13, 3 to 17, each out of 32. Sixteen distinct goals total, not 96 independent tasks.

Same answers and update count, not equal total text or compute. Extra training partly rescues the original examples. Exploratory panels.

slides.title: Reward training showed little transfer so far.
slides.notes:
One separate update per tool setting. Familiar goals were in RL training; different target roots were not. Shared recipe world.

Raw transfer gains one attempt; assisted transfer gains none. Do not compare final scores across columns. New training and SFT controls are pending.

slides.title: Does a helper improve the whole task?
slides.notes:
RLMs already delegate. Test no helper versus fixed/adaptive programmed rules, on one examined goal, twice per setting.

Shared calls, text and inventory. Helper activity is not whole-task success. This pilot does not show learned recursion or a new architecture.

slides.title: The strongest lead is better worked examples.
slides.notes:
Candidate paper: controlled teaching repair, not discovery of teacher-learner knowledge mismatch. Second-family repair is pending.

Ask which missing evidence matters most: broader transfer or explaining the effect. Helper benefit is a distinct research claim.
